title: LIMITS longitudinal study: impact of malnutrition, sarcopenia, and a TIPS insertion on prognosis in liver cirrhosis
summary:
Liver disease often results in weight loss and loss of muscle. Affected patients often suffer from malnutrition and muscle wasting, which have an unfavorable impact on the course of the disease and everyday fitness. This can affect quality of life and lead to further complications. The links between cirrhosis, malnutrition and muscle wasting are not well understood. Malnutrition and muscle wasting are often diagnosed late or not at all in liver cirrhosis because they are difficult to detect due to fluid retention and obesity.
The LIMITS study is investigating links between malnutrition, muscle wasting and liver cirrhosis in order to make improvements for affected patients. The study will focus on the impact of these conditions on the progression of liver disease. In addition, methods will be highlighted to best diagnose malnutrition and muscle wasting in liver cirrhosis patients. 
The results of the study will help us to improve the diagnosis and treatment of patients with liver cirrhosis in the future.
conditions: Other and unspecified cirrhosis of liver
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- confirmed liver cirrhosis
- consent ability
Exclusion criteria:
- Unable or unwilling to attend follow-up appointments or unable to answer questionnaires (lack of mobility, lack of compliance, e.g., due to uncontrolled search disease)
- concomitant disease (COPD GOLD 3 or 4, heart failure NYHA 3 or 4, foreseeable need for major surgery)
- Active tumor disease including HCC (pre-existing malignant tumors or reasonable suspicion (e.g., hepatic lesions LIRADS 3 or 4); curatively treated tumors including HCC with no evidence of recurrence for >3 years and non-melanotic skin cancer are not exclusion criteria)
- Criteria of an ACLF fulfilled
- Diseases affecting musculoskeletal or joint function (e.g., apoplexy with paresis)
- Condition after major amputations
- History of eating disorders (e.g., anorexia nervosa, bulimia)
- Restricted food intake or absorption due to other conditions (e.g., achalasia, feeding via PEG, need for special diets (phenylketonuria), short bowel syndrome)
- Cardiac pacemaker/ defibrillator
